title: Workflow studio: break, replay, hand over

slides.title: Deliver evidence another student can use
body: Week 10 / H3 / 60-minute lab
Core tasks first; optional challenges last.
slides.teach: Restore the H2 runtime or run the self-contained walkthrough once. Tasks1-2 were begun in H1 and Tasks3-5 guided in H2; H3 completes evidence and additional controlled tests. No new graded weekly homework is added.

slides.title: Reserve time for the actual handover
body: Task 6: 15 min; Task 7: 12; Task 8: 13.
Keep 20 min for peer explanation, export and optional work.
slides.teach: These are H3 practice allocations. Total class practice is120minutes, not120 plus a second walkthrough.
slides.visual_scope: Native teaching diagram or actual fitted-function evidence

slides.title: Restore configuration, not a remembered score
body: Locate selected candidate, versions and data hash.
Do not regenerate a preferred split.
slides.teach: The original reference selects Ridge20, but students identify their own record. If variables are missing in a new runtime, run the walkthrough in order rather than copying a number from the slides.

slides.title: Check Task 1: set versus sequence
body: ID membership can survive reordering.
Prediction comparison also needs aligned order.
slides.teach: Students explain both set recovery and ordered lookup. A test that checks only a set cannot establish that individual predictions line up with observations. The runner uses the saved test-ID sequence.

slides.title: Check Task 2: prove training-only scaling
body: Find the pipeline scaler and training means.
Stop if their values disagree.
slides.teach: This assertion is necessary for the claimed preprocessing scope, but it is not a complete leakage audit. Have the reviewer locate the actual fit call and check that validation/test targets never fit transformations.

slides.title: Check Task 3: preserve the chosen winner
body: Validation MAE and the listed tie order decide.
Do not replace it after a final-test inspection.
slides.teach: The validation winner remains fixed through Tasks4–8. The new Task6 changes only CSV row order in an explicitly reviewed copy, not the selected alpha.

slides.title: Check Task 4: read rejection messages
body: A deliberate error should be caught locally.
Unexpected acceptance must remain a failure.
slides.teach: The notebook operates on temporary copies. Reviewer verifies each case reports rejected=True and that the original CSV hash remains unchanged. Do not remove failing assertions to force a successful demo.

slides.title: Check Task 5: compare the process result
body: Use exact test IDs before numeric tolerance.
Notebook globals must not rescue missing files.
slides.teach: The exported replay process is separate from the notebook interpreter and working directory. It still shares Python packages. Passing establishes a bounded computational replay rather than independent scientific replication.

slides.title: Task 6: reorder data rows in a reviewed copy
body: Reverse CSV data rows; preserve saved ID lists.
Check every ID-keyed record before updating the copy’s digest.
slides.teach: Only the temporary copy changes. The original byte hash and chosen model remain unchanged. This is a reviewed transformation, not blind rehashing to force acceptance.
slides.visual_scope: Native teaching diagram or actual fitted-function evidence

slides.title: Task 6: different bytes can preserve the records
body: CSV row order changes its SHA256.
The full ID-keyed value mapping can still be equal.
slides.teach: Distinguish exact byte identity from record identity. Both are checked rather than assuming a matching prediction means every record is equal.
slides.visual_scope: Native teaching diagram or actual fitted-function evidence

slides.title: Task 6: test alignment after the reorder
body: A fresh process rebuilds cohorts in saved ID order.
Compare the 89-row prediction vector again.
slides.teach: The legitimate copy has an explicitly updated CSV digest after record equality is established. Its selected candidate is unchanged. OptionalA instead keeps the old digest and expects rejection.
slides.visual_scope: Native teaching diagram or actual fitted-function evidence

slides.title: Task 7: predict a coordinate response
body: Add 0.1 training SD to the bmi coordinate only.
Expected fitted response change is 0.1 times its standardized coefficient.
slides.teach: This checks the additive fitted function, not medical causation or a feasible intervention. Record which candidate is being interpreted.
slides.visual_scope: Native teaching diagram or actual fitted-function evidence

slides.title: Recover the same function in raw coordinates
body: Divide standardized coefficients by training scales.
Adjust the intercept and compare every prediction.
slides.teach: The median has no slope interpretation; if it won, the notebook explicitly inspects the separately predeclared Ridge20 candidate.
slides.visual_scope: Native teaching diagram or actual fitted-function evidence

slides.title: Check the entire response-change vector
body: Compare observed minus slope-predicted change.
An average alone can hide mismatched rows.
slides.teach: All89 differences are compared under the declared tolerance. This uses no new target labels and is not a fresh accuracy estimate.

slides.title: Task 8: verify all six payload hashes
body: The manifest must name the exact required files.
Recheck original evidence before handover.
slides.teach: Compare the manifest key set and every current digest. Missing required files and mismatched digests are errors. The manifest file itself is excluded from its own digest map to avoid a circular definition.

slides.title: An unsigned manifest is not authentication
body: Matching digests detect inconsistent copies.
A sender can replace both data and manifest.
slides.teach: Ask for an explicit attack counterexample: changing a file and its recorded digest passes a purely local consistency check. Authenticity needs a trusted out-of-band source or signature, beyond this exercise.

slides.title: Write a precise result card
body: Include task, actual result and failure ID.
Add limitation and next evaluation.
slides.teach: Students fill the controlled-change and limitation reflections. The card should distinguish model error against outcomes from replay difference between computations. A perfect replay may preserve an imperfect model.

slides.title: Prediction error and replay difference answer different questions
body: A good replay retains the original model’s failures.
Show both numbers and name what each compares.
slides.teach: Ask the student to locate one actual failure ID and the separate zero-centered process difference. Do not use a zero process difference as a model-accuracy claim.
slides.visual_scope: Native teaching diagram or actual fitted-function evidence

slides.title: Use AI for hypotheses, not fabricated runs
body: Ask for an explanation or a debugging hypothesis.
Verify against files and executed outputs.
slides.teach: No AI account is required. If used, disclose material assistance and checks. A language model cannot establish that a cell executed or invent a valid test metric. Keep decisions and evidence under student control.

slides.title: Optional A: alter a copied file
body: Append a blank line to a copied CSV.
The manifest should reject it before training.
slides.teach: The original reference remains untouched. A blank line can preserve parsed values while changing exact byte identity. The runner verifies checksums before loading/training, so the copied payload should fail as expected.

slides.title: Optional A: interpret the rejection honestly
body: Integrity checking worked for this alteration.
It did not authenticate an unknown sender.
slides.teach: The optional code catches ValueError and asserts the message identifies a checksum mismatch. It does not assert that every malicious alteration or scientific error can be detected by this manifest.

slides.title: Optional B: make an explicit name adapter
body: A positional model expects canonical feature order.
Restore names before passing values.
slides.teach: An adapter must be explicit and tested, not a silent guess. The optional code reverses feature columns in memory, maps each value back by feature name, and asserts exact recovery of the original matrix.

slides.title: Do not confuse adaptation with acceptance
body: A strict interface can reject bad order.
A reviewed adapter can produce valid order.
slides.teach: Both behaviors can be correct if their boundaries are declared. Do not weaken the original contract merely to avoid errors. An adapter also needs missing/duplicate-name handling in a real system; this controlled example uses a known unique list.

slides.title: Nineteen fields preserve your reasoning
body: Eight predictions + eight explanations + three reflections.
Blank fields produce a draft; text completeness is not correctness.
slides.teach: All response cells are pre-created. There is no need to insert cells or rerun response initialization after writing.
slides.visual_scope: Native teaching diagram or actual fitted-function evidence

slides.title: Export the handover after updating responses
body: Download one ZIP and save the edited notebook separately.
The inner reference bundle remains frozen.
slides.teach: The ZIP includes the seven-file handover directory, actual plots and the current response/evidence record. Re-export after response edits; do not overwrite a reference file to make a check pass.
slides.visual_scope: Native teaching diagram or actual fitted-function evidence

slides.title: Peer handover: locate evidence without help
body: Partner identifies the selected candidate and failure.
Then follows the readable replay instructions.
slides.teach: Pairs can download the ZIP, inspect its contents and review the source. In a compatible environment, replay can be run after extraction. Do not ask students to execute untrusted arbitrary source merely because another student sent it.

slides.title: Troubleshoot by dependency, not by score
body: Check files, IDs, feature order and versions.
Do not adjust tolerances until the cause is understood.
slides.teach: This is a diagnostic ordering, not a universal guarantee of cause. Missing dependencies, a wrong path or a stale export should be investigated before model changes. Keep the original failing evidence rather than overwriting it.

slides.title: Prepare for the written and oral exam
body: Explain your choices and one invalidating change.
The lab does not replace either examination.
slides.teach: Week11 remains the written and oral midterm. Use a two-minute explain-back with one actual result and limitation. No new exam policy, project grading or weekly assignment is introduced by this studio.

slides.title: Summary: preserve, validate, replay, explain
body: Stable IDs and frozen choices make comparisons meaningful.
A standalone reference check makes the handover inspectable.
slides.teach: Use one concrete example for identity, contract rejection, fresh-process comparison and the limits of the result.
slides.visual_scope: Native teaching diagram or actual fitted-function evidence

slides.title: Exit: explain your result without hidden notebook state
body: Locate the winner, one failure ID and the replay comparison.
State one limitation and the next needed evaluation.
slides.teach: Prepare for the written and oral midterm on16November. This is formative practice and does not replace either assessment.
